topic: Dynamic Linking and Loading with ld.so
explanation: Dynamic linking defers the resolution of symbol addresses until runtime.  The dynamic linker, ld.so (on Linux), is a crucial component that loads shared libraries (.so files) and resolves their dependencies at program startup.  It uses information embedded in the executable and shared libraries (like the program header, dynamic segment, and relocation entries) to map libraries into memory and patch addresses, allowing multiple programs to share the same library code in memory, saving space and improving efficiency.
code_example:
# Environment Variables for ld.so

export LD_PRELOAD="/path/to/hook.so"
# Forces specific library to load first

export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="/opt/custom/lib"
# Adds directories to the runtime library search path

export LD_BIND_NOW=1
# Forces resolution of all symbols at startup
# (Increases load time, safer runtime)

# Debugging the Linker

LD_DEBUG=files ./program
# Show which shared objects are loaded

LD_DEBUG=bindings ./program
# Trace symbol resolution and binding

# Utility Tool

ldd /usr/bin/program
# Lists the shared library dependencies
# (Uses dynamic linker routines for analysis)
keywords: ld.so, dynamic linking, runtime linker, shared library loading
